data.narrative:
Standard Nuclear, a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Kurt Terrani, is valued using a peer-informed triangulation against a comp universe of 11 total entities: 3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Fuse Energy, Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Oklo. The company has raised $182M to date.

Two valuation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis anchors to the $470M total-raised proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, implying $940M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Nano Nuclear Energy ($808M, Seed), Fuse Energy ($200M, Series A), and Valar Atomics ($6.0B, Series B)—yields a median of $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects early-stage sector heterogeneity and differing technology risk profiles.

Triangulating both methods produces a valuation range of $687M to $1.1B, with a median of $874M. Key uncertainties include (1) technology validation risk and path to commercialization, (2) regulatory and licensing timelines, and (3) capital intensity of scale-up. The spread between methods—$940M versus $808M—is modest (14%), supporting confidence in the $874M midpoint, though the wide peer range ($200M–$6.0B) underscores material dispersion in how the market prices nuclear development stage and technical approach.
